subject.title: [Bug] MiniMax Token Plan (Max) broken in sub-agents after v5.22 bootstrap change

question: Should OpenClaw support MiniMax Token Plan sub-agent workflows by changing the MiniMax provider route, by changing sub-agent skill/context inheritance, or by keeping the current boundary and asking Token Plan skill bundles to live outside core?
rationale: The issue mixes a possible provider/auth regression with a deliberate least-privilege sub-agent bootstrap boundary and optional Token Plan skill bundles, so automation cannot safely choose the product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep boundary, fix only live-proven bugs
options.body: Require live MiniMax Token Plan proof first, then make only narrow provider/media fixes that do not restore broad sub-agent skill inheritance.

options.title: Add an explicit opt-in skill path
options.body: Approve a documented plugin or config seam for selected sub-agent skill bundles while preserving the current default AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md boundary.

options.title: Restore broad sub-agent skill/context inheritance
options.body: Make sub-agents inherit the broader Token Plan skill context by default, accepting higher token and context-leakage risk.

recommendation.title: Keep boundary, fix only live-proven bugs
recommendation.body: Require live MiniMax Token Plan proof first, then make only narrow provider/media fixes that do not restore broad sub-agent skill inheritance.

likelyOwner.reason: Eva authored the sub-agent bootstrap boundary commit that this issue is asking maintainers to revisit.
